guitar.evidence: Atomic Rooster was primarily organ/keyboard-driven (Vincent Crane); guitarists rotated and none became iconically associated with a specific instrument.
guitar.notes: No well-documented signature gear for this band's guitarists.

tone.target: nasal fuzz lead/rhythm with wah and raw 70s drive
tone.profile: nasal fuzz lead/rhythm with wah and raw 70s drive
tone.summary: A high-gain signal chain utilizing Fuzz/Red Haze for the core tone, followed by a classic UK amp model (UK 45) to capture the Plexi/Marshall feel, finished with Wah and basic modulation.

rig.name: Atomic Rooster - Tomorrow Night - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and excessive noise inherent in fuzz/high-gain tones.
Provide the required aggressive fuzz overdrive edge and raw attack.
Implement the mandatory wah sweeps and filter movement.
blocks.gap: The GP-180 does not have a dedicated Wah module, so 'Boost' is used as a placeholder for an external/simulated wah effect (assuming it can be configured to act as a frequency sweep).

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Plexi/Marshall sound and provide classic British rock grit.
Capture the required raw 4x12 cabinet tone.
Slightly scoop the low end and boost mids for a nasal, aggressive 70s lead tone.
Added modulation for depth, but kept off to avoid washing out the raw fuzz attack.
blocks.gap: The source material is very aggressive and dry; Tremolo is optional and should be subtle or bypassed entirely.

blocks.purpose: Provide minimal natural room ambience without adding wash or delay.
blocks.gap: The source demands a 'raw mono feel,' so the reverb mix must be kept extremely low to avoid sounding ambient.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to capture the raw, aggressive 70s British rock sound.

proposals.reason: Enhance the raw, period-accurate grit and punch of a classic British rock cabinet.
